texts.preamble: Mithun Sharma vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 29 August, 2020 Author: Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari Bench: Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari High Court Of Madhya Pradesh, Bench At Gwalior M.Cr.C. No.30585/2020 (Mithun Sharma Vs The State of M.P. ) (1)
texts.facts: The applicant has filed this first application u/S 439, Cr.P.C. for grant of bail. The applicant has been arrested on 17/08/2020 by Police Station Jaura District Morena (M.P.), in connection with Crime No. 501/2019 registered in relation to the offence punishable under sections 420, 272 and 273 of the IPC and Sections 51 and 59 of the Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006. Prosecution story in short is that on 23/07/2019 Authorities alongwith the team inspected the Sharma Dairy situated at Jaura belonging to the applicant. During inspection, the Food Officer found that Panner is being prepared in the dairy and 15 kg refined HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH, BENCH AT GWALIOR (Mithun Sharma Vs The State of M.P. ) palm oil was found in the dairy. On the aforesaid basis, crime has been registered against the applicant.
texts.arguments: Learned counsel for the applicant submits that he has falsely been implicated in the matter and he is in custody since 17/08/2020. It is submitted that charge-sheet has been filed and no further custodial interrogation is required in the matter. He further submits that in case some adulterated Mithun Sharma vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 29 August, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10815250/ 1 food articles were found in the dairy then the case can not be registered under Section 420 of the IPC, when the act for storing the adulterated articles have been specifically made punishable under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act,1954. He further submits that registration of FIR Section 51 and 59 of the Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006 is also erroneous because the Act is a complete code in itself with regard to manufacturer, sale of food articles and contravention in respect thereof. Learned counsel for the applicant has placed reliance on the judgment of Division Bench at Principal Bench in M.Cr.C. No. 8629/2006 vide order dated 03/02/2010 in support of his contention. He further submits that sample was referred to Mysore Laboratory, who has also opined that Paneer is of sub standard "nature". It is further submitted that in view of outbreak of COVID 19, detention of the applicant in already congested prison may be detrimental. Conclusion of trial is likely to take time and there is no likelihood of his absconsion, if released on bail. On these HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH, BENCH AT GWALIOR (Mithun Sharma Vs The State of M.P. ) grounds, he may be released on bail. Learned Additional Advocate General opposed the application and prayed for its rejection by contending that on the basis of the allegations and the material available on record, no case for grant of bail is made out and he further submits that applicant is a habitual offender and the offence committed by the applicant is against the society inasmuch as adulterated food was manufactured which would affect the health of public at large, therefore, he prays for rejection of bail. At this stage, learned counsel for the applicant volunteered to deposit an amount of Rs. 10,000/- (Rs. Ten Thousand Only) in Prime Minister Citizen Assistance and relief in Emergency Situation Fund (PM Cares Fund). However, it would not be desirable to enter into the merits of the rival contentions at this juncture. Considering the overall facts and circumstances of the case coupled with the fact that trial is not likely to conclude in near future and prolonged pre-trial detention being an anathema to the concept of liberty, this Court is inclined to extend the benefit of bail to the applicant. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on merits of the case, this application is allowed and it is directed that the applicant HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH, BENCH AT GWALIOR (Mithun Sharma Vs The State of M.P. ) be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs. 50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with a local surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court/committal Court for his appearance on the dates given by the concerned Court. The applicant shall also furnish a written undertaking that he will abide by the terms and conditions of various circulars, as well as, orders issued by the Central Government, State Government and local administration from time to time such as maintaining social distancing, physical distancing, hygiene etc. to avoid proliferation of Corona virus. 5.
